mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand for new homes, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as broader economic demand indicators falter.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST decreases > 10%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase simultaneously, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) both decline in the same quarter, it signals a broad-based weakening of demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations diminish.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline in the same quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and RSAFS decline in the same quarter, the hypothesis is rejected.
